set_up.summary: The project can be run using Docker Compose configurations for development, local, staging, and production environments, or via makefile targets and manual setup, with Docker Compose being the most reliable method.

env_vars.name: ENVIRONMENT
env_vars.purpose: Determines application configuration (DEVELOPMENT, STAGING, PRODUCTION); used by entrypoint.sh and gunicorn.conf.py to set LOG_LEVEL and other environment-specific behaviors.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_USER
env_vars.purpose: Database username for PostgreSQL; loaded from .env file in docker-compose files and used to configure db service.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env_vars.purpose: Database password for PostgreSQL; loaded from .env file and used to configure db service.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_DB
env_vars.purpose: Database name for PostgreSQL; loaded from .env file and used to configure db service.

env_vars.name: REDIS_PORT
env_vars.purpose: Port for Redis service; defaults to 6379 if not set, used by redis service in docker-compose files.

env_vars.name: PORT
env_vars.purpose: Override for API server port; defaults to 8000 in entrypoint.sh and used by uvicorn commands.

env_vars.name: HOST
env_vars.purpose: Override for API server host; defaults to 0.0.0.0 in entrypoint.sh.

env_vars.name: WORKERS
env_vars.purpose: Number of Gunicorn workers; defaults to CPU count in gunicorn.conf.py and overridden via ENVIRONMENT.

env_vars.name: LOG_LEVEL
env_vars.purpose: Controls logging verbosity; auto-set by entrypoint.sh based on ENVIRONMENT and used by gunicorn and application logs.

files_guide.purpose: Production-grade Docker Compose configuration; uses production Dockerfile stage, disables reload, sets production logging, and runs Gunicorn via entrypoint.sh.
Development environment with hot-reload enabled for API and workers; mounts src code as volumes and uses development Dockerfile stage.
Local development override with simplified paths and volume mounts; intended for direct local testing with .env and single-context build.
Staging environment similar to dev but uses .env file for environment variables via env_file; includes dynamic PostgreSQL healthcheck using environment variables.
Multi-stage Dockerfile for building both development and production images; development stage enables hot-reload via watchfiles, production stage uses minimal image and Gunicorn.
Dockerfile for Celery worker services (worker and beat); installs poetry, builds dependencies, and runs Celery with s3-events and default queues.
Gunicorn configuration for production API container; sets bind, workers, timeout, and log level based on settings from src.config.
Entrypoint script for API and worker containers; loads .env variables, normalizes ENVIRONMENT, sets defaults (PORT, LOG_LEVEL), and validates dependencies.
Alembic migration configuration; points to migrations/ directory for version scripts and sets script location for database schema versioning.
Task runner for local development using Poetry; includes commands for installation, migration, testing, linting, and formatting.
Script to validate system dependencies (Docker, Node, Python 3.11+, AWS CLI) before running the project locally.

overview.summary: This codebase is a FastAPI-powered backend system managing GitHub integration and user authentication, structured around a modular src directory with supporting infrastructure in Terraform, Docker, and nginx. It follows a clear separation of concerns with dedicated modules for data models, configuration, migrations, and services.

risks: In-memory tracking may not scale across multiple server instances.
No persistence of rate limit state means limits reset on server restart.
IP-based limiting may block legitimate users behind shared NATs.
Lack of configurable limits per endpoint or user tier.

detail.summary: Enforces API rate limits per user/IP using middleware and in-memory tracking.
The request is initially handled by the FastAPI router dispatch, which triggers middleware chaining in order.
This step authenticates the user and populates the request state with user metadata, which is later used for rate limiting identities.
An external call to AWS Cognito is made to retrieve the signing key — failure here blocks all authenticated requests.
The get_identifier function determines whether to use user_id or remote_addr for limiting, based on config.
If user is authenticated, user_id is preferred; otherwise, falls back to IP — this impacts fairness and scalability.
The limiter uses an in-memory dictionary (e.g., defaultdict(int)) to track request counts per key — not thread-safe in production.
This handler is registered as a FastAPI exception handler and overrides default response logic for RateLimitExceeded.
Endpoints like login() or create_user() are now executed — rate limiting ensures they aren't overwhelmed by abuse.
This step is critical — if skipped or misordered, rate limits would not accumulate correctly.
The entire flow is transparent to the client — they only see success or 429, without internal state exposure.

steps.name: Request received by HTTP server
steps.description: An incoming HTTP request enters the application via the ASGI server (e.g., Uvicorn or Gunicorn).
steps.insight: The request is initially handled by the FastAPI router dispatch, which triggers middleware chaining in order.

steps.name: UserContextMiddleware processes request
steps.description: The UserContextMiddleware extracts and validates the JWT token from the Authorization header.
steps.insight: This step authenticates the user and populates the request state with user metadata, which is later used for rate limiting identities.

steps.name: decode_access_token verifies JWT
steps.description: Decodes the JWT token using the public key fetched from Cognito JWKS endpoint.
steps.insight: An external call to AWS Cognito is made to retrieve the signing key — failure here blocks all authenticated requests.

steps.name: RateLimitMiddleware applies rate limiting
steps.description: The rate limiting middleware uses the user ID or IP address to check against in-memory counters.
steps.insight: The get_identifier function determines whether to use user_id or remote_addr for limiting, based on config.

steps.name: get_identifier extracts request identity
steps.description: Extracts either the authenticated user ID or the client IP address to use as the rate limit key.
steps.insight: If user is authenticated, user_id is preferred; otherwise, falls back to IP — this impacts fairness and scalability.

steps.name: MockLimiter.checks_limit
steps.description: The MockLimiter class checks if the identifier has exceeded its configured request quota within the time window.
steps.insight: The limiter uses an in-memory dictionary (e.g., defaultdict(int)) to track request counts per key — not thread-safe in production.

steps.name: rate_limit_exceeded_handler responds to limit breach
steps.description: If the limit is exceeded, this handler returns a 429 Too Many Requests response with retry-after header.
steps.insight: This handler is registered as a FastAPI exception handler and overrides default response logic for RateLimitExceeded.

steps.name: Request proceeds to target endpoint
steps.description: If the rate limit is not exceeded, the request passes through middleware and reaches the intended API endpoint.
steps.insight: Endpoints like login() or create_user() are now executed — rate limiting ensures they aren't overwhelmed by abuse.

steps.name: Request count is incremented
steps.description: After successful request processing, the MockLimiter increments the counter for the identifier.
steps.insight: This step is critical — if skipped or misordered, rate limits would not accumulate correctly.

steps.name: Response returned to client
steps.description: The API response, with headers and body, is sent back to the client through the ASGI server.
steps.insight: The entire flow is transparent to the client — they only see success or 429, without internal state exposure.
